correctness.rationale: The definition depends only on minimal recovery sets, multiplicities and pairwise intersections. Fresh independent exact enumeration reconstructed 11 minimal recovery sets for each request. With \(L=2\), every selected service has multiplicity at most two because it intersects every copy of itself, so all possibilities lie in the finite domain \(\{0,1,2\}^{11}\) per request. Requiring at least five occurrences and the same-request exclusion bound leaves 141 candidates for each request; cross-request constraints leave 306 compatible pairs for each request pair; intersecting all three relations leaves exactly two global triples, both with totals \((5,5,5)\). This independently reproduces the frozen exhaustive certificate.
correctness.risk: The theorem is a labeled finite classification; it does not quotient the two solutions by code automorphisms.

value.rationale: This is the canonical example used by the new paper to show why multiset services matter. A complete classification showing exactly two labeled realizations is a natural finite benchmark for the new recovery model, not a random matrix census.
value.risk: It does not optimize other \((m,L)\) parameters or classify automorphism orbits.

final_claim: For the fixed labeled eight-column binary generator matrix in Example IV.22 of arXiv:2605.09748v2, there are exactly two labeled service multisets making it \((5,2)\)-strongly online, and both have exactly five service occurrences for each request.
limitations: No assertion that the two labeled solutions are inequivalent under all code automorphisms.
